# Joint base/normal moments and exact pointed critical sections

This note concerns the ACTUAL one-group full-base-rank H separator and
its affine homothetic source envelope. It records two exact interfaces:
the effective pointed-section centroid, including its normalization, and
a common source base covariance which appears at every source facet.
The covariance statement is simultaneous across normals and uses physical
base coordinates. Its source term has order epsilon; no fixed Gamma
payment or equality of quadratic moments is inferred.

Write N=d+1, K_z subset y(z)+ell(z)D, with y and ell affine, ell>0.
At each positive contact a, K_(p_a)=y(p_a)+ell_a D and Y_a=(p_a,y(p_a)).
The genuine source buffer is f_H(Y_a)=ell_a f_D, and

    delta_a=epsilon ell_a f_D, e_a=kappa_a delta_a,
    Kappa=sum_a kappa_a, pbar=(sum kappa_a p_a)/Kappa,
    ellbar=ell(pbar),
    K_base=sum_a kappa_a(p_a-pbar)(p_a-pbar)^T.          (1)

The same kappa_a come from the actual common separator. They cannot be
chosen again for different facets. All selected cap normals satisfy
Gamma(u_i)=1. Their pointed margins are ell(z)[u_i.xi+epsilon f_D].

## 1. EXACT pointed-section centroid, with the same allocations

For cap i let s_iz be its effective physical section coarea at base z,
including full proper sections and the SAME outside supporting density
from the separator; inside sections have selector zero. Put S_i=sum_z s_iz.
The signed cap-normal equations give

    sum_z z s_iz = S_i pbar,
    sum_z int X d sigma_iz
       =S_i[y(pbar)-epsilon f_D ellbar grad Gamma(u_i)].  (2)

Affine y allows subtraction before changing coordinates:

    sum_z int (X-y(z)) d sigma_iz
       =-S_i epsilon f_D ellbar grad Gamma(u_i).        (3)

Put xi=(X-y(z))/ell_z. Physical section coarea pulls back as
ell_z^(d-1) dH_(d-1)(xi)/|u_i|, with the unchanged supporting selector.
The pointed law f(xi)=sum_z ell_z^d 1_(D_z)(xi) has effective section
measure

    d s_i^point=sum_z ell_z^d tau_iz(xi)
                                      dH_(d-1)(xi)/|u_i|.

Its total coarea is exactly

    T_i=sum_z ell_z s_iz=S_i ellbar.                   (4)

Equations (3)--(4) prove the EXACT normalized identity

    (1/T_i) int xi d s_i^point
                    =-epsilon f_D grad Gamma(u_i).    (5)

It is not merely an unspecified O(epsilon) error. Euler homogeneity
checks its normal coordinate: u_i dot grad Gamma(u_i)=Gamma(u_i)=1,
so (5) lies on u_i.xi=-epsilon f_D. The result retains all original
outside selectors. It is not the centroid of an unallocated full section.

The pointed cap masses are exactly the original cap masses, since the
margin factors by positive ell_z and dX=ell_z^d dxi. The pointed total
mass is M. At epsilon=0, if the actual unbuffered source assumptions hold,
the selected pointed sections in (5) are all centered at zero.

A normalization warning about BASE means is material. Let Sigma_i^base
be the covariance of z under the ORIGINAL effective section law s_iz/S_i,
and let l=grad ell. Under the pointed coarea weighting, the base mean is

    p_i^point=pbar+Sigma_i^base l/ellbar.               (6)

Consequently l dot(p_i^point-pbar)=Var_i(ell)/ellbar>=0.
Those covariance matrices can depend on the cap. Thus there is no common
unweighted pointed base mean unless this drift is separately zero.
The exact transformed identities are instead

    E_point[z/ell_z]=pbar/ellbar,
    E_point[1/ell_z]=1/ellbar.                          (7)

Fractional labels z/ell_z are not integer labels and are not substituted
for the original lattice.

## 2. A common positive source law on ALL source facets

Let P_D(xi)=1+a_D.xi, V_D=|D| and E_D=E_D(0). The H source part of Xi is

    e_a[P_a(X)^(-N)/(N E_a)+1/(d N V_(p_a))].

On a source fiber, P_a=P_D, E_a=ell_a^d E_D, V_a=ell_a^d V_D.
After pulling its surface back to D, its EXACT measure becomes

    epsilon f_D kappa_a q_D^src(xi) dS_D(xi),
    q_D^src= P_D^(-N)/(N E_D)+1/(d N V_D).             (8)

The ell_a factors cancel completely. Therefore the positive source
surface contribution is the PRODUCT of one base measure sum kappa_a delta_p_a
and one common boundary law q_D^src dS_D. In particular the base mean
pbar and base covariance K_base are the SAME at every source facet and
every measurable subset of a source facet in pointed coordinates. This
coherence is special to the actual tied response coefficients; separate
face multipliers cannot be assigned independently.

Define the non-source response density

    C_eps(z,X)=(1/(2M))sum_i e_i sum_j rho_ij
                                      [u_ij.(X-g_z)]^2 >=0,
    Bstar=beta+(d+2)Delta/(2dM),
    R(z,X)=Bstar-W(z,X)-C_eps(z,X).                    (9)

R is a SIGNED density; it must not be declared a positive target law.
The full stress is Xi=source-density-R.

Fix a facet F of D with normal n, and put c_F=int_F q_D^src dS_D.
Let sigma_n be physical boundary area over ALL sampled fibers at this
normal, not just their outer contacts. Its source facets are part of that
measure. The affine and quadratic normal-localized tests give

    int R d sigma_n =epsilon f_D c_F Kappa,
    int R z d sigma_n =epsilon f_D c_F Kappa pbar,
    int R (z-pbar)(z-pbar)^T d sigma_n
                         >=_PSD epsilon f_D c_F K_base.  (10)

For a facet normal the disintegration has an actual atom. These identities
follow by restricting the already established normal-localized identities
to that atom; no illegal pointwise conditioning on a continuum is used.
Quadratic tests are globally convex physical fields. Every statement uses
the SAME separator and the SAME contact covariance in (1).

More generally, use any affine physical coordinate vector V_n(z,X).
The full matrix inequality is

    int R V_n V_n^T d sigma_n
       >=_PSD epsilon f_D sum_a kappa_a
             int_F q_D^src(xi)
                 V_n(p_a,y(p_a)+ell_a xi)
                 V_n(p_a,y(p_a)+ell_a xi)^T dS_D.      (11)

This is the joint base/continuous form; testing only z would discard
its cross blocks. No sign-changing normal weight is used to obtain PSD.

## 3. Exact constants for a centroid-marked regular simplex in every d>=2

Suppose D is a regular simplex centered at its centroid zero, with inradius
h>0 and facet normals n_0,...,n_d of unit length. Then a_D=0 and E_D=V_D,
so

    q_D^src=1/(d V_D).

All facet areas are A, with d V_D=N A h. The facet centroid is h n_j,
and its uniform intrinsic covariance is

    Cov(F_j)=h^2 Pi_j,  Pi_j=I-n_j n_j^T.              (12)

To verify (12), its d vertices have squared mutual edge length
2d(d+1)h^2. The uniform (d-1)-simplex covariance is
[1/(d(d+1))] times the sum of centered vertex outer products; that
sum is d(d+1)h^2 Pi_j. Thus every constant in (12) is exact.

Put L2=sum_a kappa_a ell_a^2. For this normal use the AFFINE vector

    Z=z-pbar,
    T_j=X-y(z)-ell(z)h n_j.

The source product law (8) has zero Z/T_j cross moment, because its
conditional centered facet mean is zero. Formula (11) becomes

    int R [Z;T_j][Z;T_j]^T d sigma_(n_j)
       >=_PSD (epsilon f_D/(N h))
                     diag(K_base, h^2 L2 Pi_j).       (13)

Thus an endpoint-density construction which deletes the full base
covariance or chooses unrelated base source laws on different facets
cannot satisfy the actual H equations. There is a compulsory identical
base block at every one of the N facet normals.

One can also aggregate in common continuous coordinates. Let

    U_j=X-y(z)-ellbar h n_j,
    Var_ell=sum_a kappa_a(ell_a-ellbar)^2=l^T K_base l.

The regular-simplex identities sum n_j=0 and sum n_j n_j^T=(N/d)I
cancel the SOURCE mixed base/continuous blocks after summing j. Hence

    sum_(j=0)^d int R [Z;U_j][Z;U_j]^T d sigma_(n_j)
       >=_PSD diag( (epsilon f_D/h)K_base,
          (epsilon f_D h/d)[(d-1)L2+Var_ell] I ).      (14)

The left mixed block has NOT been separately set to zero. Inequality
(14), including that actual left block, is what the simultaneous tests
prove. For a nonregular simplex, retain (11), or apply a common continuous
affine normalization while transforming normals, covariance, and surface
Jacobians consistently. A marked point different from the centroid uses
(8)--(11); the uniform simplification (12) is then unavailable.

## 4. Exact gap/covariance constraints, and a sign warning

For each normal define the affine nonnegative envelope gap

    g_n(z,X)=ell(z)h_D(n)-n.(X-y(z)).

Full physical affine tests give int g_n Xi=0. Quadratic tests give the
positive-semidefinite block matrix

    int [Z;g_n][Z;g_n]^T (-Xi) d sigma_n >=_PSD 0.     (15)

Its cross block int Z g_n(-Xi) need not vanish. In scalar base direction
a, (15) gives the exact Cauchy bound

    [int (a.Z)g_n(-Xi)]^2
      <=[int (a.Z)^2(-Xi)] [int g_n^2(-Xi)].           (16)

The measure -Xi is signed, but its full quadratic form is PSD by the
actual convex tests. Neither factor on the right may be replaced by an
unweighted variance. Only an additional proved zero factor would force
the cross block to vanish.

On actual boundaries g_n equals the convex base support defect
ell(z)h_D(n)+n.y(z)-h_(K_z)(n). The boundary martingale preserves g_n,
and its row support equality forces equality in Jensen for that convex
base defect. Thus a source row at g_n=0 remains on the true outer footprint;
other rows remain in affine regions of that defect. This statement does
not force their gap variance in (16) to vanish.

## 5. A diagnostic for the exact section identity: genuine nested marginals

The following ordinary projected example shows why (5), even with actual
convex nested fibers and genuine projected maxima, is not itself a Gamma
bound. It does NOT have a full-rank deepest source hull or actual global
mixed criticality, and so is not a counterexample to the proposed full
interface.

In barycentric coordinates on a d-simplex D, let g=(1/N,...,1/N) and
for i=0,...,d define the positive parallelotope

    K_i={lambda in D: 0<=lambda_j<=1/N for all j!=i}.

Its volume is v_d V_D, v_d=d!/N^d. It lies in D and contains g at one
vertex. For an integer L>=1 define the ordinary density

    f=1_D+L sum_i 1_(K_i),
    M_f=V_D[1+L N v_d].

The canonical caps H_i={lambda_i>=1/N} each have EXACT mass

    Q_f=V_D[Gamma_d+L v_d].                            (17)

They cover all continuous space, so maximum depth is at most Q_f.
At g, every halfspace captures at least Gamma_d V_D from D. Couple the
N uniform K_i points by cyclically permuting one uniform K_0 point.
Their sum is N g pointwise. Thus any through-g halfspace contains at
least one coupled point, giving total K_i capture >=v_d V_D. This proves
the matching lower bound Q_f for EVERY direction. Hence g is an actual
ordinary deepest point and

    Q_f/M_f=Gamma_d-
       [L v_d(N Gamma_d-1)/(1+L N v_d)] < Gamma_d       (18)

for d>=2. Every proper central canonical section is centered at g.
The outside K_j facets on its plane also have aggregate centroid g
under equal selectors across j!=i, by permutation symmetry. Thus the
effective section centroid condition survives.

For L even this is the pointed marginal of an ACTUAL complete family:
use base P={0,+-e_1,...,+-e_(LN/2)}, put D at base zero, and put paired
copies of each K_i at the corresponding opposite vertices. The integer
points of this crosspolytope are exactly P. Its canonical hull has the
listed fibers: every nonzero label is exposed, and all other fibers
contributing at zero lie in D. Thus compatibility and nestedness are real.
Its source core at zero has base rank zero, not full rank.

The missing actual MIXED criticality can be detected explicitly. For the
canonical cap i, vary the base tilt along one coordinate whose two opposite
fibers both carry K_i. A sufficiently large tilt changes their contribution
from 2|K_i| to |K_i| while leaving the central proper cap and all other base
traces unchanged. Thus (17)'s cylindrical cap is not globally minimizing
at the mixed source. The first-order outside supporting capacities may
still satisfy the tilt-zonotope test: that test is necessary, not sufficient.
This exact diagnostic keeps the extra global-tilt obligation visible.

## 6. Current consequence and remaining payment

Equations (5), (10)--(16) are actual invariants of the one-group H interface.
They genuinely couple the same source base moments across the facets and
retain every supporting allocation. The source covariance in (13)--(14) is strictly positive when the
POSITIVE-kappa contact bases have full affine base rank. A full-rank
assigned source face alone does not ensure that all its contacts receive
positive kappa, and even full rank gives no uniform eigenvalue floor along
a sequence. Its coefficient is O(epsilon).
This alone supplies no uniform Gamma-scale contradiction as epsilon tends
to zero; positive target spread can pay a small covariance cost.

No exact compatible full-rank-source configuration has been shown to
violate these invariants, and no proof is claimed that they exclude all
facet endpoint concentrations. A successful next step must bound the
actual residual base/support covariance or use global cap-tilt minimality,
rather than assuming a quadratic equality or a vanished mixed block.
